title: Add RecipeImageLoader async helper
description: Create RecipeImageLoader.swift with an async function (or actor) that accepts a recipe source-file URL obtained from the security-scoped bookmark established in 0003. It searches for a sibling file sharing the same base name with extensions .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .heic (in that order), calls startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() before reading, and stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() in all exit paths (success and failure). Returns a SwiftUI Image on success or nil when no sibling exists.
acceptance_criteria: startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() is called before any file-system access.
stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource() is called in all exit paths.
Extensions are tried in order: jpg, jpeg, png, heic.
Returns nil without throwing when no sibling image exists.
Returns a non-nil Image when a valid sibling is found.

handoff_summary.completed: Created CookbookApp/Recipes/RecipeImageLoader.swift: namespace enum RecipeImageLoader with static async func loadImage(for:) -> Image?. Security-scoped access is bracketed with start/stop via defer. Extensions are iterated in spec order. Returns nil when no sibling exists, SwiftUI Image when one is found. Syntax-checked clean.
handoff_summary.remaining: None for this bead. Downstream tester bead should verify: start called before FS access, stop called on all paths (success, nil-sibling, each loop iteration), extension ordering, nil return for missing sibling, non-nil return for present sibling.
handoff_summary.risks: RecipeThumbnailView currently loads images without security-scoped access (it runs within RecipeDiscovery.scan's active scope). If RecipeImageLoader is called independently (outside an active folder scope), startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() on a non-bookmarked file URL will return false and reads may fail silently. Callers must ensure the folder scope is active, or RecipeImageLoader should accept the folder URL instead. This is a pre-existing design ambiguity — not introduced by this bead.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should write unit tests verifying all five acceptance criteria, particularly the security-scoped resource call ordering and the nil/non-nil return paths.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None. RecipeImageLoader.swift is a new file with no overlap with existing files. No existing file was modified.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used a namespace enum (matching RecipeDiscovery pattern) rather than an actor or class, since the loader is stateless. Used Task.detached(priority: .utility) for file I/O off the main thread, matching RecipeThumbnailView's approach. Followed RecipeDiscovery.scan's defer-guarded start/stop pattern. startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() is called on the recipe URL (the security-scoped resource), not on each candidate image URL, so one start/stop pair covers all sibling checks.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests written — tester agent's responsibility. Key test cases: (1) no sibling → nil; (2) jpg sibling present → Image; (3) extension ordering (jpeg preferred over png when both exist would actually pick jpg first per ordering); (4) start called exactly once before fileExists; (5) stop called when start returned true on success and on nil path.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: If the recipe URL passed in is not itself a security-scoped bookmark (i.e., it was obtained by enumerating a folder's bookmark scope), startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() will return false and stop will not be called. File reads will still succeed as long as the caller holds the folder scope open. This mirrors the existing RecipeThumbnailView behavior.

conflict_risks: None. RecipeImageLoader.swift is a new file with no overlap with existing files. No existing file was modified.

Implementation follows the same pattern as RecipeDiscovery.scan. Compiled cleanly with swiftc -typecheck against the iOS simulator SDK.
